name: Austin Pacheco
location: Based in Atlanta, GA — available for remote & on-site work
statement: I cut for rhythm first, story second — the two are rarely in conflict once you find the right frame to hold on. Six years across narrative shorts, music videos, and commercial work.

editing.title: Night Drive
editing.description: A neon-soaked 18-minute short about two strangers sharing a rideshare through downtown Atlanta after midnight. I cut 14 hours of handheld footage into a tight, rhythmic piece that lives and dies on the pacing of silence between dialogue. Premiered at Atlanta Film Festival 2025.

editing.title: Harvest
editing.description: Feature-length documentary following three generations of peach farmers in rural Georgia. I handled the full offline-to-online pipeline in DaVinci Resolve — assembly, fine cut, color grade, and deliverables. 87 minutes, 200+ hours of source footage.

writing.title: The Last Diner
writing.description: A feature screenplay about a waitress at an all-night diner who discovers her regulars are not who they seem. Noir-tinged drama with dark comedy beats. Currently in development with Faultline Pictures.
writing.script:
FADE IN:

INT. LUNA'S ALL-NIGHT DINER — NIGHT

Fluorescent tubes hum over red vinyl booths. A jukebox in the corner plays something slow and forgotten. The clock above the grill reads 2:47 AM.

MARLENE (34), sharp eyes behind tired makeup, tops off coffee for BOOTH 4 — an OLD MAN in a wool coat who has been here every night this week.

MARLENE
Same time tomorrow, Mr. Calloway?

CALLOWAY
(without looking up)
That depends on whether tomorrow comes.

Marlene pauses. Laughs it off. Moves on.

She passes BOOTH 7 — a YOUNG WOMAN (20s) typing furiously on a laptop, surrounded by crumpled napkins.

MARLENE
Refill?

YOUNG WOMAN
(not looking up)
I'm rewriting the ending. Again.

MARLENE
Of what?

YOUNG WOMAN
Everything.

Marlene glances at the screen. We catch a fragment: a police report. Crime scene photos. This is not fiction.

The BELL above the door RINGS. A man in a soaked raincoat steps in. He doesn't sit down. He scans every booth.

MARLENE (V.O.)
I used to think the late shift was boring. That nothing real happens after 2 AM. I was wrong.

SMASH CUT TO:

INT. LUNA'S ALL-NIGHT DINER — LATER

The diner is empty. Every booth. Every stool. Marlene stands alone behind the counter. The jukebox has stopped. The clock reads 2:47 AM. Still.

FADE OUT.

writing.title: Neon Silence
writing.description: Award-winning short screenplay. A deaf teenager navigates a loud house party for the first time. Told almost entirely without dialogue — the audience experiences the party through vibration, light, and body language. Won Best Short Screenplay at Peachtree Film Awards 2024.
writing.script:
FADE IN:

INT. SUBURBAN HOUSE — NIGHT

Bass vibrates through the walls. We HEAR it — a thumping, distorted pulse. Then:

SILENCE.

We are inside JADE's world now. JADE (17), curly hair pulled back, stands at the front door. She presses her palm flat against the wood. Feels the music.

She opens the door.

INT. LIVING ROOM — CONTINUOUS

A wall of bodies. Mouths move but we hear nothing. Lights strobe. Red cups rise and fall. Someone is laughing — we see it in the way their shoulders shake, their head thrown back.

Jade steps in. She moves through the crowd like water around stones.

A BOY bumps into her. His mouth moves — an apology, maybe. He holds up a cup toward her. She shakes her head. Smiles.

She finds a corner. Leans against the wall. Closes her eyes.

We FEEL the bass through the wall behind her. A deep, rhythmic pulse.

Her fingers tap against her thigh. In time. She's dancing. Just her fingers.

A GIRL (MIKA, 17) slides into the space next to her. Mika doesn't speak. She just leans against the same wall. Closes her eyes too.

Their fingers find each other.

The bass pulses on.

FADE OUT.

TITLE CARD: NEON SILENCE

lighting.title: Glasshouse
lighting.description: Music video for indie band Half Light. Shot in an abandoned greenhouse using only practical lights — 200 string lights, 40 candles, and two 1K tungsten Fresnels bounced off mylar sheets. No HMIs, no LEDs. All warmth.

lighting.title: Parallel Lines
lighting.description: Live theatrical production at The Fox Theatre, Atlanta. Designed a lighting plot with 64 fixtures across 4 acts. Heavy use of gobo projections and color temperature shifts to mark time-of-day transitions in a play set entirely in one room.

camera.title: Concrete Orbit
camera.description: 60-second national spot for an Atlanta-based sneaker brand. Shot on ARRI Alexa Mini with Cooke S4 primes. Handheld street photography aesthetic — we followed real skaters through Woodruff Park at golden hour across two shoot days.

camera.title: Salt Flats
camera.description: Independent feature shot on location in Bonneville, Utah. Operated A-cam (RED Komodo, Sigma Cine lenses) across a 22-day shoot. Primarily Steadicam and dolly work for wide landscape compositions.

camera.title: Stillwater Portraits
camera.description: Ongoing personal photography series. Environmental portraits of people in small Georgia towns, shot on medium format film (Mamiya RB67). Published in Atlanta Magazine, Southern Living.
